pointers.sentence: The uploaded files are subclasses of it ([Upload handlers and uploaded files](../http/uploads.md#uploadedfile-and-its-subclasses)), and so is a file field's `FieldFile` ([File fields](../models/files.md)) (`django/core/files/base.py:File`).

The mixin also gives `closed`, true when there is no wrapped object or it is closed, and `readable`, `writable` and `seekable`, with an answer for an object that lacks them (`django/core/files/utils.py:FileProxyMixin`).
A `File` is true in a boolean context, with a name or without one (`django/core/files/base.py:File.__bool__`).

`FieldFile` and `UploadedFile`, with the upload classes under it, keep the older test, true only when the name is not empty: an instance whose file field is empty still has a `FieldFile`, which `FieldFile._require_file` tests before the file is used (`django/db/models/fields/files.py:FieldFile.__bool__`).
A `File` used to be true only when its name was not empty (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
The size is a `cached_property`, so writing through the wrapped object's `write` does not change it (`django/core/files/base.py:File.size`).

`File.chunks` is a generator that rewinds the file with `seek(0)` where it can, then reads it `File.DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE` bytes at a time, 64 KiB unless a size is passed, until a read returns nothing, so a file that has been partly read is still read whole (`django/core/files/base.py:File.chunks`).
`FileSystemStorage` writes a file from its chunks when it has no temporary file to move (`django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:FileSystemStorage._save`).

`File.multiple_chunks` answers whether the size exceeds one chunk; no code in Django calls it, and `InMemoryUploadedFile` answers false whatever its size (`django/core/files/uploadedfile.py:InMemoryUploadedFile.multiple_chunks`).

A line ends in `"
"`, `"
"` or a lone `""`, and a `""` at the end of a chunk is held too, until the next chunk shows whether a `"
"` follows it (`django/core/files/base.py:File.__iter__`).
It returns the `File`; leaving a with statement on it calls `File.close`, which closes the wrapped object (`django/core/files/base.py:File.open`).
`ContentFile.write` writes at the stream's current position, the start for a new one, and drops the size, so that the next request for it seeks to the end (`django/core/files/base.py:ContentFile`).

`ImageFile` is a `File` with `ImageFile.width` and `ImageFile.height`, read together once and kept; to read them it opens the file, and closes it again if it was closed before (`django/core/files/images.py:ImageFile._get_image_dimensions`).

A file that runs out first, or a path that will not open, gives `(None, None)`, and an open file is put back where it was, or closed when close is true (`django/core/files/images.py:get_image_dimensions`).

`validate_file_name` raises `SuspiciousFileOperation` for a name whose last part is empty, `"."` or `".."`, and, unless relative paths are allowed, for any name with a directory in it; when they are, for an absolute path or one that climbs with `".."` (`django/core/files/utils.py:validate_file_name`).

The module `django.core.files.locks` gives `lock`, with `LOCK_EX` or `LOCK_SH`, and `LOCK_NB` added for a lock that does not wait, and `unlock`, each taking a file object or a descriptor (`django/core/files/locks.py`).

When the rename fails, as it does across file systems, it copies in chunks into a destination opened exclusively, unless overwriting is allowed, and locked, then gives it the source's permissions and times and removes the source (`django/core/files/move.py:file_move_safe`).

`NamedTemporaryFile` in `django.core.files.temp` is the standard library's everywhere but Windows, where it is a class of Django's own, made with mkstemp and deleting its file when it is closed (`django/core/files/temp.py`).
